text:
Monzo is the strongest overall pick for a UK current account that combines budgeting with saving pots: it offers spending categories, real-time notifications, round-ups, pot locking, and pots that can be used to pay bills. Starling is the best close alternative if you prefer a simpler, free account with useful pots/spaces and bill budgeting.
becleverwithyourcash

Best options
Bank	Best for	Budgeting and pots	Watch-outs
Monzo	Best all-round budgeting + pots	Pots, round-ups, spending categories, bill pots, pot locking, transaction notifications	Some premium features require a paid tier; easy-access pot rates can change
Starling	Simple, free everyday budgeting	Spaces/pots, spending insights, ability to set money aside for bills	Fewer advanced budgeting extras than Monzo
Monzo + separate savings account	Best if interest matters	Use Monzo for budgeting, then move longer-term savings to a competitive easy-access saver or ISA	Adds a little admin
Traditional bank with pots	If you want a high-street bank	RBS/NatWest offer pots, but RBS says its pots do not earn interest	Usually less sophisticated budgeting than Monzo/Starling

Monzo’s app lets you categorise spending, receive transaction alerts, round up purchases into a pot, lock a pot for a chosen period, and assign a pot to cover regular bills—making it particularly good for a “pay yourself first” budget. Starling and Monzo both let you segregate money into separate pots and assign one to pay bills directly.
becleverwithyourcash

My recommendation

Choose Monzo if you want one app to run your whole monthly budget: salary, bills pot, spending categories, round-ups, and separate goals.

Choose Starling if you want a clean, free account and do not need Monzo’s more advanced budgeting features.

Keep the bulk of savings elsewhere if you are saving for months or years: a pot is primarily an organising tool, and some banks’ pots pay no interest. RBS, for example, explicitly says its pots do not earn interest.
rbs.co

A practical setup would be: Monzo for everyday spending and a bills pot; then move money you will not need soon into the best easy-access savings account or Cash ISA you can find. Monzo also provides access to partner savings products, but compare the current rate and FSCS protection before committing.
moneyzine

Important checks

Confirm whether the account and any pot/savings feature are free, and whether a paid plan is worthwhile for you.

Check FSCS eligibility: for Monzo and Starling, eligible deposits are protected up to £85,000 per person, per banking licence.

Do not treat a budgeting pot as a substitute for a proper emergency fund or a competitive savings account.

Interest rates and promotional offers change frequently, so verify the live rate before opening an account.
which.co
